_comment: Backend comparison query set, used by scripts/compare_backends.py to fill
the measured-numbers table in docs/splunk-vs-azure-monitor.md.
BOTH sides are captured automatically. Azure via the App Insights query
API; Splunk via POST /v2/signalflow/execute on stream.<realm>.signalfx.com,
which is plain HTTP Server-Sent Events and terminates on its own when
given immediate=true with a bounded start/stop. Credentials come from
.env, exactly as the dashboard REST scripts do.
THREE THINGS THAT MAKE A NAIVE SIDE-BY-SIDE TABLE WRONG, all measured:
1. UNITS DIFFER, AND NOT JUST BETWEEN BACKENDS. Splunk's service.request
histogram is in NANOSECONDS, while its own traces.span.metrics.duration
is in MILLISECONDS (that unit is set by the span_metrics connector
config). Azure's requests.duration is milliseconds. splunkScale below
normalises everything to milliseconds. Without it, Service Overview
latency reads 1000x high.
2. A PERCENTILE CANNOT BE COLLAPSED BY AVERAGING. Taking the mean of
per-interval P90s is not the window P90 -- the same error trap 22
records for standard deviation. Asking SignalFlow for one
window-wide bucket also produced a boundary artefact (a spurious
1.44e9 point). So percentile rows compare the MEDIAN OF PER-INTERVAL
percentiles on both sides, and the Azure KQL is written to compute
exactly that. Apples to apples, and honest about what it is.
3. DISTINCT-COUNT IS NOT THE SAME QUESTION ON BOTH SIDES. Azure's dcount
is a true distinct count over the window. Splunk's dimensional metrics
can only give a distinct count per interval, so the best available is
the peak. Those are different statistics and the row says so. This is
the log-backed versus metric-backed distinction, not a defect.
4. SPLUNK service.request DOUBLE-COUNTS WITHOUT filter('sf_dimensionalized',
'true'). It emits an endpoint-level MetricSet carrying that property AND a
service-level one where the property is absent; summing both counts every
request twice. Measured: 132 unfiltered vs 66 filtered vs 58 in Azure over
the same window. Ratios such as error rate escape it because both halves
double; counts do not. This was a live defect in splunk/dashboard.json.
splunkAggregate: sum | median | max | mean | ratio
ratio expects the program to publish labels 'errors' and 'total', and
divides the summed series rather than averaging per-interval ratios.

rows.kql: requests | where cloud_RoleName == 'rag-api' | summarize v = sum(itemCount) | project tostring(v)
rows.splunkflow: A = histogram('service.request', filter=filter('sf_service', 'rag-api') and filter('sf_environment', 'dev') and filter('sf_dimensionalized', 'true')).count().sum().publish(label='v')
rows.expectation: Match expected. Both count the same server spans.

rows.kql: requests | where cloud_RoleName == 'rag-api' | summarize t = sum(itemCount), e = sumif(itemCount, tobool(success) == false) | project tostring(iff(t == 0, 0.0, round(100.0 * e / t, 2)))
rows.splunkflow:
F = filter('sf_service', 'rag-api') and filter('sf_environment', 'dev') and filter('sf_dimensionalized', 'true')
A = histogram('service.request', filter=F and filter('sf_error', 'true')).count().sum().publish(label='errors')
B = histogram('service.request', filter=F).count().sum().publish(label='total')
rows.expectation: Match expected. Summed then divided, not averaged per interval.

rows.kql: requests | where cloud_RoleName == 'rag-api' | summarize p = percentile(duration, 50) by bin(timestamp, 1m) | summarize v = round(percentile(p, 50), 1) | project tostring(v)
rows.splunkflow: A = histogram('service.request', filter=filter('sf_service', 'rag-api') and filter('sf_environment', 'dev') and filter('sf_dimensionalized', 'true')).percentile(pct=50).publish(label='v')
rows.expectation: Median of per-minute P50. Splunk service.request is NANOSECONDS, scaled to ms.

rows.kql: requests | where cloud_RoleName == 'rag-api' | summarize p = percentile(duration, 90) by bin(timestamp, 1m) | summarize v = round(percentile(p, 50), 1) | project tostring(v)
rows.splunkflow: A = histogram('service.request', filter=filter('sf_service', 'rag-api') and filter('sf_environment', 'dev') and filter('sf_dimensionalized', 'true')).percentile(pct=90).publish(label='v')
rows.expectation: Divergence expected: Splunk interpolates within histogram buckets.

rows.kql: requests | where cloud_RoleName == 'rag-api' | summarize p = percentile(duration, 99) by bin(timestamp, 1m) | summarize v = round(percentile(p, 50), 1) | project tostring(v)
rows.splunkflow: A = histogram('service.request', filter=filter('sf_service', 'rag-api') and filter('sf_environment', 'dev') and filter('sf_dimensionalized', 'true')).percentile(pct=99).publish(label='v')
rows.expectation: Largest divergence expected, for the same reason.

rows.kql: dependencies | where cloud_RoleName == 'rag-api' | where tostring(customDimensions['gen_ai.operation.name']) == 'chat' | summarize p = percentile(duration, 90) by bin(timestamp, 1m) | summarize v = round(percentile(p, 50), 1) | project tostring(v)
rows.expectation: span_metrics duration is ALREADY milliseconds, so no scaling. Divergence from bucket interpolation: LLM latencies land in the 2s-to-5s bucket.

rows.kql: dependencies | where cloud_RoleName == 'rag-api' and name == 'db.vectorSearch' | summarize p = percentile(duration, 50) by bin(timestamp, 1m) | summarize v = round(percentile(p, 50), 1) | project tostring(v)
rows.expectation: Both read the same span durations in ms; divergence from interpolation only.

rows.kql: customMetrics | where name == 'gen_ai.client.token.count' and cloud_RoleName == 'rag-api' | where tostring(customDimensions['gen_ai.token.type']) == 'input' | summarize v = tolong(sum(valueSum)) | project tostring(v)
rows.splunkflow: A = data('gen_ai.client.token.count', filter=filter('gen_ai.token.type', 'input') and filter('service.name', 'rag-api'), rollup='delta').sum().publish(label='v')
rows.expectation: Match expected. Both sum a delta counter over the window.

rows.kql: customMetrics | where name == 'gen_ai.client.token.count' and cloud_RoleName == 'rag-api' | where tostring(customDimensions['gen_ai.token.type']) == 'output' | summarize v = tolong(sum(valueSum)) | project tostring(v)
rows.splunkflow: A = data('gen_ai.client.token.count', filter=filter('gen_ai.token.type', 'output') and filter('service.name', 'rag-api'), rollup='delta').sum().publish(label='v')
rows.expectation: Same. Note the dashboard chart hardcodes a 4h window; this query does not.

rows.kql: dependencies | where cloud_RoleName == 'rag-api' and name == 'db.vectorSearch' | summarize v = sum(itemCount) | project tostring(v)
requests | where cloud_RoleName == 'rag-api' | extend s = tostring(customDimensions['session.id']) | where isnotempty(s) | summarize v = dcount(s) | project tostring(v)
rows.splunkflow: A = data('traces.span.metrics.calls', filter=filter('service.name', 'rag-api') and filter('span.kind', 'SPAN_KIND_SERVER') and filter('session.id', '*')).sum(by=['session.id']).count().publish(label='v')
rows.expectation: NOT THE SAME STATISTIC. Azure is a true distinct count over the window; Splunk's dimensional metrics can only count distinct per interval, so this is the peak. Splunk <= Azure is expected and correct, not a defect. See section 6.
